Computes the mean curvature of a scalar field from its Hessian trace, normalized by the gradient magnitude.
It sets itself apart by incorporating gradient normalization for surface smoothness regularization.
Choose it when optimizing SDFs for surface smoothness. [Link](3126-mean-curvature-grid-computation.md)
Computes the divergence of a vector field on a grid.
It sets itself apart by operating on vector fields rather than scalar fields.
Choose it for fluid simulation or vector field analysis. [Link](3151-divergence-grid-computation.md)
Computes the Laplacian (trace of the Hessian) of a scalar field.
It sets itself apart by using finite difference stencils directly on the grid values.
Choose it for standard grid-based SDFs without neural feature grids. [Link](3160-laplacian-grid-computation.md)
Regularizes depth and image gradients using first-order derivatives.
It sets itself apart by focusing on 2D image/depth space rather than 3D volumetric space.
Choose it for monocular depth estimation or image processing. [Link](6439-depth-and-image-gradient-regularization.md)
Computes the Laplacian using adjoint operators to implicitly define boundary conditions.
It sets itself apart by avoiding explicit padding and handling boundaries via interior gradients.
Choose it when boundary artifacts from padding are problematic. [Link](8252-laplacian-grid-computation-via-finite-differences.md)
Computes the Eikonal equation's omega term for regularization.
It sets itself apart by enforcing the eikonal constraint on the gradient magnitude.
Choose it for SDF regularization in neural rendering. [Link](13240-eikonal-omega-term-computation.md)
*   **Time Complexity**: $O(1)$ per query point, as it involves a fixed number of arithmetic operations on the 8 vertices of the enclosing voxel.
*   **Memory Complexity**: $O(1)$ auxiliary memory per query point.
*   **Strengths**: Provides exact analytical second derivatives for trilinear interpolation, enabling precise regularization of SDF gradients in neural rendering pipelines.
Avoids the numerical instability of finite differences.
Does not handle non-linear interpolation kernels.
Requires manual implementation in frameworks lacking double back-prop support for grid samplers.
*   **When to use**: When optimizing neural feature grids for SDFs (e.g., in GO-Surf) and gradient regularization is needed.
*   **When not to use**: When using other interpolation methods (e.g., bilinear, cubic) or when the SDF is defined by a neural network without a feature grid.

It was developed to address the lack of support for double back-propagation through PyTorch's grid sampler, which is essential for regularizing the gradient term of the SDF during the optimization of neural feature grids.

The technique is specific to the GO-Surf architecture and has not been widely adopted in other volume rendering methods, which typically rely on finite differences or auto-diff on the final scalar field.
